fields.v: Feng, Z., Zhang, R., Yang, Y., Xie, P. (2026). The Missing Complement: State-Conditioned Minimal Sufficient Evidence for Coding Agents. arXiv:2609.20050v3 [cs.IR], 19 Nov 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2609.20050v3 [cs.IR], 19 Nov 2026 (pages headed 'Preprint'); no published venue found (no journal_ref in the arXiv export, not in the other exports)
Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of California San Diego (all four authors)

Proposes an approach; secondary: Proposes an evaluation method — MSS-COMPLEMENT, a training-free state-conditioned evidence-set retrieval method for coding agents, plus the task formulation and the SERBENCH benchmark (500 test + 500 development states); the method is evaluated and compared against 11 retrievers, ablations and downstream cohorts
fields.why: Form now right. Main vs secondary is still a judgement: the paper lists three equal contributions (task formulation, SERBENCH, MSS-COMPLEMENT, p. 3); the method is the headline result, but the benchmark with expert certificates is an equally large part of the paper
fields.doubt: O artigo apresenta três contribuições iguais (tarefa, SERBENCH, MSS-COMPLEMENT). Decide se a natureza principal é 'Proposes an approach' (método) ou 'Proposes an evaluation method' (benchmark).

fields.v: MSS-COMPLEMENT (authors' own; Cal500-frozen configuration). Compared retrievers: BM25, BGE-large, SPLADE++, ColBERTv2, ReasonIR-8B, SweRankEmbed-Large, Qwen3-Embedding-8B, Qwen3-Embed + Reranker-8B (+MMR), AgentIR-4B, Agent-ModernColBERT; SSR (authors' one-pass set reranker); AMA-Agent on AMA-Bench

Portable state card (issue, current need, search history, opened files, observations, failures, hypothesis, subgoal); candidate pool of code units; returned set of 4-8 intact code units within 6,144 source tokens. Benchmark side: grouped-MSS certificate (groups of acceptable evidence IDs with threshold, necessity weight, role; enumerated branches), hidden from methods. No specification artefact for code generation

Nine-view deterministic ranking of the pool (BM25 x4, TF-IDF x2, dense, entity, recency) fused by RRF (<=384 candidates) -> Call 1 proposal (DeepSeek-v4-pro, 8-unit set S0 from <=80 cards) -> Call 2 gap-directed expansion (DeepSeek-v4-flash, <=48 candidates) -> Call 3 finalization (DeepSeek-v4-flash, 4-8 units) -> renderer applies token budget (Fig. 3)

None in the method. Benchmark certificates: two human experts review all 500 states, senior expert adjudicates; independent audit of 80 states. Action52: a human reviewer labels executor targets precise/coarse/wrong
Single mechanism: evidence (context) selection at one agent decision; downstream effect tested at one repair-localization decision (Action52) and in an end-to-end repair loop (Fresh23)
Not classifiable (context retrieval for coding agents; no specification; authors do not use SDD terms)
Existing code bases: issue resolution in real repositories (Multi-SWE-bench, SWE-bench-Live issues); states captured mid-trajectory

Automatic: organizer scorer against private certificates; repository tests in Fresh23; LLM judge (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) for AMA correctness. Manual: certificate annotation and review by experts (with model audit signals from Grok 4.6, Gemini 3.6 Flash, Claude Sonnet 5); human labelling of Action52 targets. 95% intervals by 20,000 repository-clustered paired bootstrap resamples

Per-state success criterion stated by the authors: a returned set is complete only if it covers every certificate group (Complete-MSS@k, Test500); in Fresh23 a task is resolved when fail-to-pass tests pass (strict: pass-to-pass also). No threshold for a configuration as a whole is stated, so no verdicts: quality and cost 'no criterion stated by the authors' for every entry. No coding agent is evaluated on Test500 (retrieval methods). (1) MSS-COMPLEMENT (controller DeepSeek-v4-pro + DeepSeek-v4-flash): Complete-MSS@5/@8 73.00 / 80.60; group recall@5 82.03; mean 2,543 source tokens @5; 41.50K controller tokens per state, about 1.5 US cents. (2) Qwen3-Embed + Reranker-8B: 61.40 / 72.40 (36.24% @5 on states with >=3 groups); 2,721 source tokens @5. (3) Other baselines Complete-MSS@5: BM25 9.00, BGE-large 31.00, SPLADE++ 23.60, ColBERTv2 16.80, ReasonIR-8B 28.00, SweRankEmbed-Large 52.40, Qwen3-Embedding-8B 52.60, AgentIR-4B 38.60, Agent-ModernColBERT 34.00. (4) Ablations (Test500, Complete@5): independent similarity 66.60; no feedback fixed 7 69.80; no feedback adaptive 72.80; single-stage 70.00; no expansion 72.60. (5) Full-repository diagnostic, Complete@5: MSS-COMPLEMENT 38.80 vs Qwen3+Reranker 33.80. (6) Action52 fixed-budget target precision, DeepSeek-v4-flash executor: Qwen3 Embed 48.54, Qwen3+Reranker 51.46, MSS-COMPLEMENT 64.33, Oracle-1 group 52.63, Oracle-MSS 64.91; Claude Sonnet 5 executor: 54.39, 54.39, 58.48, 55.56, 66.67. (7) Fresh23 strict / F2P resolved of 23 (executor DeepSeek-v4-pro on 20 tasks, v4-flash on 3): BM25 5/8, Qwen3+Reranker 6/10, MSS-COMPLEMENT 8/10, Oracle-1 group 7/8, Oracle-MSS 8/11; executor tokens per task 133,775 / 126,261 / 118,351 / 98,121 / 99,655. (8) AMA-208 accuracy: MSS-COMPLEMENT 56.05% vs AMA-Agent 53.97%; online tokens per question 33.57K vs 13.95K. (9) Prospective44 controller family, Complete@5: DeepSeek 45.45 vs Claude 52.27 (Claude run $5.78)

Tasks: Test500 states with frozen candidate pools (each contains a complete set); secondary cohorts Action52, Fresh23, AMA-208, Prospective44, full-repo diagnostic. Compared: MSS-COMPLEMENT vs 11 retrievers + ablations. Baseline: strongest = Qwen3-Embed + Reranker-8B. Held constant: same states, pools, scorer; configuration frozen on Cal500; retriever query choice fixed on a 75-state Cal500 subset; temperature 0; in Action52/Fresh23 same executor, evidence count, token ceiling. Acceptance: hidden expert-reviewed certificates; repository tests (Fresh23). Repetitions: single run per method, bootstrap intervals; post-freeze parameter neighbourhood on Cal120. Human intervention: none at inference

MSS-COMPLEMENT best on Test500: +11.60 points Complete-MSS@5 over Qwen3+Reranker [+6.89, +17.21], +8.20 @8 [+4.91, +13.85]; +14.09 on >=3-group states vs +7.41 on single-group; matches the reranker's completeness with 40% fewer source tokens (3,655 vs 6,100). Over similarity control +6.40 [+3.42, +10.46]; feedback adds 0.20 (n.s.). Full-repo +5.00 [+1.62, +9.44]. Action52: +12.87 precision under DeepSeek (significant), +4.09 under Claude (n.s.); removing one required group -12.28 / -11.11 (significant). Fresh23: all paired intervals include zero. AMA: +2.08 [-0.16, +4.37], n.s.

Distinguished methods clearly on Test500 with repository-clustered intervals; downstream cohorts mostly underpowered (Fresh23 n=23). Repeatable: frozen configuration, released scorer, network-disabled replay reproduced predictions byte for byte; post-freeze neighbourhood within 2.5 points. Limitations stated: all test states from one trajectory generator; candidate pools contain a complete set by construction (selection, not discovery); end-to-end effect diluted by executor and environment; latency deployment-specific

One trajectory generator (adaptive_llm_trace_v3_agent); other generators and state formats untested; candidate discovery is the main bottleneck in full-repository setting; end-to-end benefit not established (Fresh23 n.s.); acquisition computation exceeds answer-context savings in AMA online total. No dedicated threats-to-validity section (short scope/limitations appendix H)

fields.why: The study evaluates 11 third-party retrievers and AMA-Agent besides the authors' own method; §5 gives Partly when the author is vendor of only some of the approaches evaluated (same reading as other own-method-vs-third-party-baseline drafts)

fields.v: Partly (0.5): training-free, API controller at about 1.5 US cents per state, requirements stated (Python/PyTorch environment, structured-output endpoint); but it presupposes a candidate pool, and with candidates from the whole repository discovery is the main bottleneck (38.8% complete); dense views and the strongest baseline rely on 8B models served locally
fields.why: Cost (about 1.5 US cents per state, p. 8) and tools are within reach, but the method assumes a supplied candidate pool; with whole-repository candidates it completes only 38.8% and the authors call discovery the main bottleneck (p. 9)
fields.doubt: Custo e ferramentas estão ao alcance (1,5 cêntimos por estado), mas o método pressupõe um conjunto de candidatos já fornecido. Decide entre Yes e Partly.
